gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long each recommended unit runs a lighting load: at ChatGPT's own 50 W × 6 h example, the River 3 Plus delivers about 249 Wh (286 Wh × 87% measured), which is about 5.0 h or 0.83 of a night, so it fails the example. The DELTA 3 Classic's measured 17 W inverter idle draw means a 20 W LED string runs about 28 h on it, not the 42 h that capacity × efficiency would suggest.
standout_why: Of the pages ChatGPT got, I checked only the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus manual (manuals.ecoflow.com, which came back with no spec text) and ChatGPT's own answer. The answer gives a generic sizing rule (50 W × 6 h = 300 Wh, so pick at least 400 Wh) but no runtime for any named product and no inverter idle draw, and it then recommends the 286 Wh River 3 Plus for patio lights, which goes against its own rule. I could not open gearranking.com (SSL error), the BLUETTI AC70 page, the EcoFlow store pages (HTTP 429) or Lowe's (HTTP 403). Gearranking advertises 'Tested Capacity' for the River 3 Plus and may already have a measured usable-Wh figure, so I scored 2, not 3.
decides: This changes the pick. On ChatGPT's own example load (50 W for 6 h), the River 3 Plus is not enough for one night, while the DELTA 3 Classic ($459 at EcoFlow US today) covers about 2.5 to 2.8 nights at about $0.54 per usable Wh. For small LED strings, the 17 W idle draw is the biggest loss, so the page should tell shoppers to add the idle draw to the light wattage before dividing.

findings.label: Measured inverter efficiency
findings.source_title: EcoFlow River 3 Plus power station – The Solar Lab
findings.note: The Solar Lab (Cody & Robbie): 'Pushing the 600W inverter, we were able to measure an 87% efficiency rating.' This was measured near full load, so efficiency at a 50 W light load is probably lower.

findings.label: Rated capacity and weight
findings.source_title: EcoFlow River 3 Plus Review – The Solar Lab
findings.note: Specs as listed by The Solar Lab ('Battery Capacity: 286Wh (expandable up to 858Wh…)', 'Weight: 10.4 lbs'). 286 Wh / 10.4 lb = 27.5 Wh/lb.

findings.label: Usable AC energy (derived)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow River 3 Plus power station – The Solar Lab
findings.note: 286 Wh × 0.87 = 249 Wh. Upper bound, because efficiency was measured at high load.

findings.label: Runtime at ChatGPT's 50 W × 6 h lighting example (derived)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow River 3 Plus power station – The Solar Lab
findings.note: 249 Wh / 50 W = 5.0 h; 249 / 300 Wh per night = 0.83. Upper bound, because idle draw is not counted.

findings.label: Measured inverter efficiency
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic portable power station – The Solar Lab
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'We measured this unit to have right around an 83% inverter efficiency.' The test load is not stated.

findings.label: Measured idle draw, inverter on
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic portable power station – The Solar Lab
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'We measured the idle draw to be roughly 17W per hour' (they mean 17 W). The same page lists the weight as 27 lb, so 1,024 Wh / 27 lb = 37.9 Wh/lb.

findings.label: Price, EcoFlow US store
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic Portable Power Station (1024Wh)
findings.note: From storecheck.py on the Shopify store, in stock. ChatGPT showed $479 at Best Buy.

findings.label: Nights at 50 W × 6 h (derived)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic portable power station – The Solar Lab
findings.note: Efficiency method: 1,024 × 0.83 = 850 Wh / 300 = 2.8 nights. Idle method: 1,024 / (50 + 17 W) = 15.3 h / 6 = 2.5 nights.

findings.label: Runtime for a 20 W LED string (derived)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic portable power station – The Solar Lab
findings.note: 1,024 Wh / (20 + 17 W) = 27.7 h. Capacity × efficiency alone would give 1,024 × 0.83 / 20 = 42.5 h, so idle draw costs about 35% of runtime at this load.
